drafted_from: tool:export-editor-timeline's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json, tools/media-composition/do-work/export-editor-timeline.mjs, tools/media-composition/do-work/export-xmeml.mjs and export-xmeml.md, and the script run on a two-cut edit
start_here: Say to your AI: "Export my two-cut bakery edit as a timeline file I can open in Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve." It runs tool:export-editor-timeline and saves the xmeml file in your files.
no_lists_because: It turns the edit you hand it into one timeline file and keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Write the edit as JSON with encode {width, height, fps} and spine.segments of clips; each clip's source is the absolute path your editor will find the recording at (not a file identity).

2. Optionally give source_metadata, keyed by that path, with fps, duration, width, height and has_audio, so the timeline is exact; without it the export lists what it assumed. Give a title for the sequence name (default Edit).

3. Say "Export this edit as an editor timeline" and the AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:export-editor-timeline. The door runs it in a container and answers {"result": {...}}; an error comes back as {"error": "what to change"}.

4. Read result.limitations (what the timeline could not carry, such as colour or caption styles) and files.timeline, the xml saved in your files; open it in your editor. A retimed or repeated clip is refused in words rather than exported wrong.
